items.title: UK's former ambassador to US arrested as Epstein files fallout continues
items.description: Peter Mandelson, a political powerbroker and former government minister, has been investigated by London's Metropolitan Police for around three weeks over allegations of misconduct in public office.

items.title: Australia first in Commonwealth to back removing Andrew from line of succession
items.description: Prime Minister Anthony Albanese tells his British counterpart, Sir Keir Starmer, that Australia would support the removal of Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor from the line of succession.

items.title: 'Could bring down Charles': Royal biographer's warning over Andrew's emails
items.description: The scandal surrounding Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor has the potential to end the reign of King Charles III, claims a British historian who wrote an unofficial biography of the former prince.

items.title: 'He's not going to get it': Trigger that could reignite Trump's Greenland bid
items.description: A former chief analyst with the Danish Defence Intelligence Service warns diplomatic efforts to settle the Greenland dispute will fail.

items.title: 'Your word against his': Women's complaints against surgeon dismissed by regulator
items.description: Australia's medical regulator, AHPRA, faces criticism for failing to act on complaints from patients about surgeries by Melbourne gynaecologist Simon Gordon.

items.title: Trump's trade tantrum may drive Canada and Australia closer
items.description: Canberra's decision to sign a bilateral agreement with Canada to join forces on everything to do with critical minerals could prove to be a forerunner of things to come.

items.title: Australian businesses warn tariff chaos becoming harder to endure
items.description: Business representatives have warned all Australian exporters they will need to monitor US trade policy carefully over coming weeks and months, as one firm owner estimates tariffs have cost him $1 million.

items.title: Her son enlisted to fight for Ukraine. In a way, his death brought relief
items.description: Ruslana Bronovytska's son Dima did not tell her he was signing up to fight for Ukraine. When he went missing, it was the beginning of a new, hellish reality many people in the country face.

items.title: Staffing crunch threatens urgent care clinic sustainability
items.description: An independent review finds Labor's urgent care clinics face workforce shortages and problems with after-hours services, with no evidence hospital waiting times have improved.

items.title: The royal commission into antisemitism starts today. How did we get here?
items.description: A landmark royal commission begins today to probe the prevalence of antisemitism in Australia and shed light on the events surrounding the Bondi Beach terror attack.

items.title: DV attacker photographed victim giving evidence, found guilty of contempt of court
items.description: A man standing trial for domestic violence charges took an image of the victim while she was giving evidence and recorded the prosecutor inside the court building, a court has heard.

items.title: Horses whistle while they whinny to produce a unique sound
items.description: The sound of a horse's whinny is created by the low frequency vibration of vocal cords combined with a high frequency whistle, a new study reveals.

items.title: Rob Reiner's son Nick pleads not guilty to murder of parents
items.description: Nick Reiner has pleaded not guilty to two counts of first-degree murder in the fatal stabbing of his parents in December last year.

items.title: Live: High-speed rail could be 'shovel ready' in two years, government says
items.description: Construction of Australia's first high-speed rail line could start as early as 2028, as the government injects an additional $229.6 million into the project. Follow live.

items.title: How 19 years on Play School fed into Simon Burke's latest role
items.description: After five years starring in major musicals, Simon Burke returns to a much smaller stage in a one-man play, on its 50-year anniversary: The Elocution of Benjamin Franklin.

items.title: The difference between homebirth and freebirth and why it matters
items.description: Experts say creating awareness around how homebirthing and freebirthing differ is important in helping women make informed and safe decisions.

items.title: Quiz: Your dog is ready for the dog park. Are you?
items.description: Dog parks can be fabulous places for socialising your pets and building community. But not all dogs are suited to a frolic with four-legged friends in off-leash areas.

items.title: Is China opening a police station inside a Solomon Islands school?
items.description: Authorities in Solomon Islands deny claims that Chinese police will run a new police post in Honiara’s Chinatown district, but say Chinese police will instead "visit" the site.

items.title: Vonn reveals amputation scare after Olympics crash left leg 'in pieces'
items.description: Lindsey Vonn credits her orthopaedic surgeon for being in Italy in the nick of time to save her left leg after her nightmare crash at the Winter Olympics.

items.title: Trump Tower for Gold Coast a magnet for the wealthy but some not so keen
items.description: A $1.5 billion Trump-branded skyscraper proposed for Surfers Paradise is being pitched as a major luxury tourism and investment draw for the Gold Coast, though some locals and visitors say the name could turn people away.

items.title: Hobart stadium power options uncosted, not finalised
items.description: Major upgrades to Hobart's power grid to supply the Macquarie Point stadium are yet to be finalised or costed, with the final estimate for the precinct's energy demand increasing by almost 50 per cent in a year.

items.title: Duterte launched 'systematic attack' on Philippine civilians, ICC prosecutors say
items.description: An International Criminal Court prosecutor tells judges that former Philippines president Rodrigo Duterte personally instructed members of a death squad to kill suspected criminals and drug users.

items.title: Sydney to Newcastle high-speed rail to be 'shovel-ready' in two years
items.description: The federal government adds fresh funds to the hundreds of millions of dollars spent planning for a high-speed rail line between Sydney and Newcastle, pledging to have the project shovel-ready within two years.

items.title: Matildas coach wants to show they're a 'dominant force' at Women's Asian Cup
items.description: Matildas coach Joe Montemurro, who has had nine months in charge leading into the Women's Asian Cup starting this week, has bold ambitions for the tournament and the future of women's football.

items.title: Cleary's ban overturned as father acts as counsel at NRL judiciary
items.description: Ivan Cleary's legal prowess comes in handy as his son, Panthers star Nathan Cleary, sees his two-match suspension overturned at the NRL judiciary.
